title: Procurement priority & trigger scorecard — regional lead times and business triggers
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a compact priority scoring framework and trigger ladder for GPU procurement across regions and SKU families. Goal is to convert operational signals (lead times, on-hold orders, utilization pressure) into deterministic procurement actions (order, lease, escalate to vendor/diversify). This is intentionally pragmatic — mix of quantitative signals and business-trigger overrides so product/infra can align to SLAs and release roadmaps.

Summary of approach:
- Signals: median and p90 lead time (days), current rack-level availability fraction (0–1), 12-week burn projection, business priority (customer features + enterprise SLAs), vendor concentration (single-vendor risk).
- Score: normalized 0–100. Higher => higher urgency to procure or secure capacity.
- Triggers: mapping from score bands to actions (immediate PO, schedule order, activate lease swap, open vendor escalation).
- Run cadence: weekly recompute; + ad-hoc recompute when product pushes/pulses > 20% forecast increase.

Scoring formula (working, tunable):
priority_score = round( (BP*0.45) + (AvailScore*0.25) + (LeadtimeRisk*0.20) + (VendorPenalty* -0.10) )
Where:
- BP (Business Priority) 0–100 (assigned by product/ops per release calendar; defaults: enterprise feature=90, managed tenants ramp=75, internal infra experiments=30).
- AvailScore = (1 - regional_backlog_fraction) * 100 (100 = fully available capacity, lower = less).
- LeadtimeRisk = min(100, (p90_lead_days / target_lead_days)*100) capped at 100 (target_lead_days = 45 for standard SKUs, 30 for common A-series).
- VendorPenalty = 0 if >2 independent vendors in region, 15 if single vendor, 7 if two vendors but shared supply chain.

Sample dataset (CSV style):
region,sku,median_lead_days,p90_lead_days,availability_fraction,burn_12w_estimated_units,business_priority,vendor_count,priority_score
us-west,gpu-a100-80,32,60,0.62,240,90,1,84
us-east,gpu-h100-80,18,28,0.88,120,75,2,73
emea,gpu-a100-40,45,90,0.40,360,85,1,91
apac,gpu-bf16-30,25,40,0.72,90,30,3,57

Interpretation notes for sample:
- EMEA A100-40: high burn and long p90 -> score 91 -> immediate action (see trigger mapping).
- US-West A100-80: moderate availability but high burn -> contingency order + start vendor outreach.
- APAC BF16: lower business priority -> monitor and consider short-term lease vs order.

Trigger ladder (deterministic mapping):
- 85–100: Immediate PO + expedite shipping lane (air freight reserved), open vendor escalation, reserve dedicated staging capacity, alert Sales/CS (potential SLA exposure). Owner: procurement lead.
- 70–84: Schedule PO on next cadence (within 2 weeks), secure 2x vendor quotes, enable conditional lease pool (30–60 day), notify product for possible feature gate. Owner: infra ops.
- 55–69: Pre-order (30–90 day horizon), maintain waitlist, enable spot-lease fallback. Owner: capacity planner.
- <55: Monitor weekly, no new committed spend; consider lease-swap if short-term spike.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Lease swap flow: if score in 55–69 but near-release (BP bumped by product), initiate short-term lease (3–8 weeks). Priority to vendors with regional presence to avoid cross-region shipping.
- Vendor diversification: whenever VendorPenalty > 10 and priority_score > 70, procurement must solicit alternate vendor proposals and present 2 feasibility options within 7 days.
- Cost trade: compute effective cost per GPU-day including freight/priority fee vs lease rate. Use a 12-week horizon for comparison.

Embedded sample table: cost comparison (example numbers):
option,unit_cost_usd,shipping_usd,lead_days,lease_weekly_usd,12w_total_cost
Buy-standard,12000,1500,45,NA,13500
Urgent-air,12000,4500,10,NA,16500
Lease-short,NA,NA,7,650,5460

Decision heuristics extracted from sheet: 
- If urgent-air premium < 25% of lifetime value of blocked customers for next quarter -> approve air.
- If buy cost + time-to-service > 12 weeks and product-critical -> prefer lease then convert to buy mid-cycle.

Operational dashboard columns expected for automation (sheet-friendly):
- region, sku, on_hand_units, reserved_units, in_transit_units, pending_po_units, median_lead_days, p90_lead_days, burn_12w_forecast, business_priority, vendor_count, priority_score, recommended_action, next_owner, action_deadline

Action items (owners / due):
- Compute automated weekly score pipeline from procurement feed + VENDOR API (Marco Li) — due 2024-10-12 (WIP).
- Add product-priority tagging in backlog so BP can be auto-ingested (Aisha Patel) — due 2024-10-19.
- Build short-term lease vendor list with contact SLA and cost sheet (Daniel Green) — due 2024-11-02.
- Run PG test of scoring sensitivity across weightings and publish recommended weights (Priya Shah) — due 2024-11-15.

Unresolved / discussion points:
- Should we weight burn_12w more heavily for GPU families where model fine-tuning is concentrated? (example: A100-80 used by most internal eval clusters)
- How to incorporate spot-price signals from cloud providers as a negative pressure (can temporarily reduce procurement urgency)?
- Define explicit approval threshold for finance sign-off (suggest 100k+ incremental spend needs FP&A).

Notes on data inputs and reliability:
- Lead times: blend of vendor-reported ETA and historical delivery distribution (we use median & empirical p90 from our 18-month rolling window). Avoid single latest ETA when variance is high.
- Availability fraction: computed as (on_hand + in_transit + pending_lease_capacity) / forecasted_required_for_12w. Fill missing fields with conservative 0.5 until data sanity checks pass.

Quick links and references:
- procurement playbook (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Procurement+Playbook
- weekly procurement board (Jira): PROJ-4123

Appendix: sample sensitivity grid (how priority changes with weight shift) — glue table for the sensitivity analysis pipeline.

End of sheet — working draft.

Comments: please add suggestions inline. This sheet is designed to be exported to CSV and ingested into the procurement automation job (weekly run). The numeric columns must remain consistent with the dashboard spec above to allow downstream mapping.
